correctness.rationale: The nonzero factorizations uv^T with v^Tu=0 have free scalar orbits of size q−1 and all belong to one Jordan class. Fix X=e_1 e_2^T and set a=s_2, b=t_1 for Y=st^T. Then [X,Y]=a e_1 t^T−b s e_2^T and tr(XY)=ab. No nonzero contraction gives rank zero, exactly one gives rank one and square zero, and two give rank two by independence of the two image vectors and two covectors. In the last case span(e_1,s) carries eigenvalues ab,−ab and the two covectors' common kernel complements it, even when the eigenvalues coincide in characteristic two. For fixed a≠0, imposing t_1 and t^Ts=0 imposes two independent scalar conditions, so the count with fixed nonzero ab is q^(2n−3); with b=0 it is q^(n−1)(q^(n−2)−1). The other one-sided count follows by transpose and swapping coordinates 1 and 2. Subtraction from the full class size gives the zero count. The sandwich identities give [C,X]=2ab X and [C,Y]=−2ab Y. If ab≠0, on span(e_1,s) the two generators have opposite off-diagonal entries and C is nonzero diagonal, so they are independent even in characteristic two. In the one-sided case C shares one image or covector line with X and the other with Y; using the distinct lines gives independence. Therefore the span is the stated three-dimensional Lie algebra whenever C≠0; the commuting case reduces to the scalar-multiple test. Normalizing by the full class size gives the stated limits. Independent replay `python3 -B /workspace/review_checks.py 5` enumerated the ambient matrices for (q,n)=(2,2),(3,2),(5,2),(2,3),(3,3), checking rank, trace, eigenspace sizes and Lie span against the proof. The trace in the finding is tr(XY), not the trace of C, which is always zero.
